title: North Providence planning board weighs part-time status for tree warden role
text:
← Back to the wire
Government
North Providence planning board weighs part-time status for tree warden role
Tree Warden Tim Thorp told the board he has been paid $25 a week for a while as the town looks for more funds.
The North Providence Planning Board discussed whether to specify in a proposed tree ordinance that the town's tree warden position is part time, during a hearing Thursday, Oct. 15, at North Providence Council Chambers.
THE QUESTION OF HOURS Board member Lou Dukio asked whether the ordinance should state that the position is part-time. Tim Thorp, Tree Warden for North Providence, said it does not have to be, noting that in Providence "there's a whole team of people that are involved in these duties." A board member suggested that leaving the language open "gives us the option."
A SUGGESTED FIX A board member proposed that, similar to how compensation is handled, the ordinance could state that the number of hours the position requires "shall be established by the mayor and the town council." Thorp agreed that would work, but added, "I will say that like largely the position is volunteer."
PAY AND BUDGET Thorp said the budget for his position is set by the town council, with the mayor proposing it. He told the board, "He he was getting $25 a week for a while. We're looking for more funds." A board member responded, "So much and thank you for the hard work," adding that "the time he spends is worthwhile."
NO RECOMMENDATION YET The board indicated it was not prepared to issue a recommendation on the compensation and hours language that night. A board member said the board would like the boundaries for hours to be established in the ordinance itself before weighing in further, saying the issue could be revisited once Thorp provides a document detailing the ordinance's proposed changes.
